title: Best Haul From a Tree of Houses
statement:
Houses are laid out as a binary tree; each node's value is the cash in that house. You may pick any set of houses, but never two houses that are directly connected: if you take a node, you can take neither its parent nor its children.

Return the largest total cash you can collect.

examples.why: Take 4 and 5 (the two children). Taking the root gives 3 + 1 + 3 + 1 = 8, which is less.
Take 4 and 3. Taking whole levels fails here: 4 sits on level 2 with nothing else, and 3 sits on level 1.
Take 10 and both 6s: grandchildren may be taken together with their grandparent.

hints: For one node there are two cases: you take it, or you skip it. What does each case allow for its children?
If you take a node, its children must be skipped. If you skip it, each child is free to be taken or skipped, whichever is better.
Have the recursion return a pair: (best if this node is taken, best if it is skipped). Combine the two pairs from the children in O(1).

explain.intuition:
This is the "no two neighbours" problem from a row of houses, moved onto a tree. Each node only needs two numbers from below: the best total of its subtree if it is taken, and the best if it is skipped.

Taking a node forces both children to be skipped: take = val + left.skip + right.skip. Skipping a node leaves each child free: skip = max(left.take, left.skip) + max(right.take, right.skip). A post-order walk computes both values for every node once, so the whole thing is linear.
steps: Write dfs(node) that returns [take, skip]; an empty child returns [0, 0].
Recurse into the left and right child first.
pitfalls: Summing alternating levels. In [2, 1, 3, null, 4] the best set mixes levels 1 and 2.
Writing the plain recursion max(val + grandchildren, children) without caching. Each node gets recomputed from its parent and grandparent, which blows up on deep trees.
Assuming a skipped node's children must be taken. Skipping both a node and its child is sometimes best, as in [4, 1, null, 2, null, 3].

complexity.space: O(h) for the recursion, h = tree height

solutions.title: Take-or-skip pair per node
solutions.idea: Post-order DFS returning (best if taken, best if skipped) for each subtree.

solutions.title: Iterative, children before parents
solutions.idea: List nodes in BFS order, then process them in reverse so every child is finished before its parent. Same recurrence, no recursion depth limit.

followups: Return which houses to take, not only the total.
The houses form a general tree with any number of children. Does the recurrence change?
